| Surface | Cost delta and limits |
|---|---|
| Tell-before-withdraw | `http/directory.rs:1037-1096` retains the existing serial FYI attempt per queued request, then scans the results and builds untold diagnostics. It processes the whole list before refusing, not just until the first failed hold. A failure now returns before the withdrawal transaction; the prior commit/pointer/route-notification work may already have landed. The same explicit command retries; no new retry timer or second commit is added. Stable `<request-id>.withdrawn` IDs still dedupe notices, though retries still pay formatting, registry/hold checks and attempted writes. |
| Gone requester | `tell_withdrawn` classifies the existing hold's unknown/tombstoned error; it adds no separate registry lookup. The handler collects/clones gone request IDs for the existing owned withdrawal task and result. Matching event payloads gain one boolean, without another event or transaction. |
| **Gone-list scaling note** | `store/role_requests.rs:392` uses `withdrawal.gone.contains` for every withdrawn row. For Q requests and G gone IDs this adds O(QG) string comparisons under the SQLite transaction and role gate, potentially quadratic when G grows with Q. Heap copying follows G ID bytes plus the existing Q notice/result bodies. The large-backlog latency qualification therefore remains material. |
| Retired-needs classification | `directory.rs:467-487` partitions already-parsed needs against the existing role/standing vectors, finds their retired targets and filters prompts. These are repeated in-memory searches, not new role/step file reads or database queries. Work grows with needed-role and role counts. Absent-role add prompts retain their previous path. |
| **Retarget construction** | `picture.rs:541-614` scans the parsed step documents once per retired-role recommendation. Its `section` helper clones each document's steps array (`83-91`), so repeated processing also copies step data even before filtering completed steps. Each matched step searches the retired list for replacements and linearly deduplicates its next-needs vector. CPU can grow with retired roles x steps x needs, plus repeated replacement/dedup scans; peak memory retains the existing parsed snapshot, a cloned section and generated strings. |
| Printed edits | `ddocs set` lines are constructed and shell-quoted, not executed by the view. There is one line per affected step **per retired-role recommendation**. When one step names several retired roles, multiple recommendations can carry the same complete replacement command; output bytes and construction work repeat. The snapshot still reads/parses each source step file once, and no blueprint/step write is introduced. |
| Invariant and test changes | The drain failure and boot-recovery additions are comments: gate/query/recovery scheduling is unchanged. The `/bin/sh printf` round-trip launch is solely in the regression test, not a runtime repair path. |

The notice guard can shorten a failed operation by skipping withdrawal, but it does not bound the preceding per-request fanout or writer wait. Successful processing retains the prior same-role gate lifetime through the owned write; no new whole-operation timeout or queue-size cap is supplied.
